transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net customer support. My name is Chloe. How may I assist you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello Chloe. I'm calling about our home telephone. We've got a terrible crackling and buzzing on the landline that's making it almost impossible to hear anything.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can certainly help you get that crackling telephone line sorted out today, George. May I start by confirming your full billing address and your security question for account verification?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, of course dear. The address is 27 Willow Crescent, Cheltenham, GL51 8PX. And my security question is my first school, which was St Mark's Church of England.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you very much, George. That matches our records perfectly. Now, please tell me a bit more about when you first noticed this buzzing noise on the line.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Well, it started about four days ago, but yesterday it got noticeably louder. My wife Margaret has a red medical alarm pendant linked to the phone line, so whenever there's a loud buzz I get terribly anxious that if she has a fall, the alarm won't dial through to the warden.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I completely understand how worrying that must be with Margaret's emergency pendant on the line, George. We treat medical care alarms as top priority, so let's get this thoroughly checked and secured for you right away.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you so much Chloe, that's such a comforting relief to hear.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Just to make sure I have the full picture: you have a loud static crackle and buzzing on the landline that worsened over the last few days, and you need to ensure the medical alarm line remains clear and operational. Is that right?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, that is exactly the problem.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Understood. First, I am going to register both of you on our Priority Services Register right now so your account is permanently flagged for priority network support.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Oh, that is wonderful. Does that mean engineers come out quicker if the line ever goes down?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, exactly. It gives you free priority fault repair within four hours and an emergency backup dialer if needed. That is all saved on your account profile now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: God bless you dear, that gives me huge peace of mind.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now, let's look at the telephone equipment inside the house. What type of telephone handset are you speaking to me on right now?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's an ordinary corded British Telecom handset with large push buttons, plugged into the main hallway socket.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And are there any other telephone extension sockets or other equipment plugged in around the house, like in the bedroom or living room?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: We have an old extension socket in the dining room with an external bell ringer chime, and an extension upstairs in the spare bedroom, though nothing is plugged in upstairs.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Obviously internal extension bell-wiring can degrade over time and pick up electrical interference that causes this exact type of crackle, George. So I'd like us to test the master socket directly.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right, I understand. What do I need to do with the hallway socket?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Take a look at that main socket in the hallway. Does it have a horizontal seam across the middle with two small screws on the bottom half?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes it does, two small cross-head screws on the lower half of the plastic box.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That is an NTE5 master socket. If you gently unscrew those two screws, the front faceplate pulls off, revealing a hidden test socket inside.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hold on just a moment, I've got my little spectacles and a screwdriver in the hall drawer.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Take all the time you need, George. I'm right here with you on the line.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right, I'm unscrewing the left screw now... and the right screw. Both screws are out.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now slide the bottom faceplate gently outwards. You will see a small socket on the right-hand side of the backplate.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes! The front plate came forward and I can see another socket behind it.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Brilliant. Now unplug your corded telephone from the front faceplate, and plug it directly into that hidden test socket.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Unplugging from the front plate... and pushing the plug into the test socket. There, it clicked in firmly.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now pick up the receiver, put it to your ear, and listen to the dial tone. How does it sound?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Lifting the receiver to my ear... heavens above! The loud buzzing hiss is completely gone. The dial tone is completely smooth and silent behind the tone.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That is fantastic news. While you have the receiver up, is the dial tone still completely clear of any crackle or static when you tap the cable?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I'm jiggling the curly wire and tapping the lead... no, absolutely silent, just a clean steady dial tone.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That confirms that the copper cable coming from the exchange down your street is in perfect condition, George. The crackle was coming from the old dining room extension bell-wire attached to the faceplate.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Good gracious, all this worry because of an old dining room wire!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It happens very frequently with older wiring, George. What I am going to do is order a brand new pre-filtered master faceplate for you. It replaces the old front plate and isolates extension wiring permanently.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And will Margaret's medical alarm unit plug straight into that without any bother?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, absolutely. The new faceplate has two separate filtered sockets: one specifically for your corded phone and one for the medical alarm box.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And how much will that replacement faceplate cost us, dear?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: It is completely free of charge under your Priority Services package, George. We never charge our priority customers for line protection equipment.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: You really are an angel Chloe. That takes such a huge load of worry off my shoulders.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I'm delighted to help. Now, before we wrap up, I'd like to do a live ringback test to verify that inbound call audio is completely clear.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right, how do we do that test?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Please place your handset down on the cradle for five seconds. My automated test line will ring your number, and when you pick up, we will speak again.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Placing the receiver on the cradle now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Triggering the ringback test now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It's ringing! Picking up now... hello, Chloe?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Hello George! I can hear your voice loud and clear, with zero static or buzzing. How is the clarity on your end?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It sounds as clear as a bell. Not a single pop or hiss. I haven't heard the telephone sound this clear in years.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Wonderful! So to recap: your telephone audio is confirmed crystal clear via the master test socket, your new filtered faceplate will arrive by Royal Mail on Thursday, and your Priority Services registration is active.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is everything sorted beyond my expectations. Margaret and I can sleep easy tonight knowing the emergency line is safe.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That is wonderful to hear, George. Is there anything else at all I can help you with today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No thank you dear, you've done everything brilliantly.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net, George. Please give my warmest regards to Margaret, and take good care.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Chloe. Goodbye now.
